subject: Supplier exit: pricing comparison and migration support
messages:
From: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supplier change — can Redwood match incumbent economics?

Hi Karthik,

We're starting an RFP run because our current supplier announced they're sunsetting a key SKU at the end of Q3. Attached is the RFP and our current contract summary. The incumbent has offered a mixed proposal: lower list price on embeddings but no migration credits and a tiered volume rebate.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you match or beat the incumbent's list + rebate structure for Year 1?
- Do you offer migration credits (one-time) or onboarding assistance for vendor replacements?
- Any packaging caveats (minimum commitments, different metering for embeddings vs. tokens)?

We'd like to present a short list to Procurement by next Tuesday. Can we set a 30-min call tomorrow?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Wong
Head of AI Procurement
Acme Corp

Attachments: Acme_RFP_2026.pdf (pdf, 480KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Supplier change — can Redwood match incumbent economics?

Hi Lisa — thanks for the context and the RFP. I can do a 30-min slot at 11:30 PT tomorrow. I've looped in Lauren to confirm commercial flexibility.

High-level answers up front so Procurement has something to consider before the call:
- We can match list price on embeddings for the first 12 months if Acme commits to a 12-month minimum spend (we'll outline thresholds on the call).
- Migration credits: we offer a one-time migration credit structured against committed spend (usually expressed as a % of the first-year commit). We also provide an onboarding package (two SRE days + dedicated SE support for the cutover).
- Packaging: embeddings and token generation are metered separately. We can offer blended unit pricing in a committed plan; otherwise they remain on standard per-request metering.

I'll follow up after our internal pricing review with a proposed line-item offer. For tomorrow's call, please confirm attendees and primary success metrics (cost, latency, runbook SLAs).

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme replacement pricing grid + playbook

Karthik / Sergio — I pulled together a quick replacement pricing grid and a short playbook for migration credits. See attachments. Highlights:

- replacement_pricing_grid.xlsx: shows incumbent pricing (as shared by Acme) vs two Redwood offer tiers (Conservative Match, Aggressive Match). Includes blended embeddings option.
- playbook_notes.md: recommended negotiation script and constraints (min commit, rebate schedule, Exclusions: audit logs charges, private deployment fees).

Recommended commercial approach (short):
1) Lead with Aggressive Match for Year 1: match list + 8% migration credit applied as a credit against the Year 1 committed invoice. Requires 12-month minimum commit at 70% of historical spend.
2) If Procurement pushes back, fall back to Conservative Match: match list price but no migration credit; offer 60-day free SE onboarding and 10% professional services discount.
3) Tie SLA concessions to defined performance SLAs (99.5% regional uptime, 95th pct latency targets) rather than blanket discounts.

Notes: Acme is very sensitive to packaging complexity — simplify to two line items: Embeddings (per-embed unit) and Generative (per-token). Avoid multi-tier rebates in the initial offer; Procurement dislikes complex accounting.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: replacement_pricing_grid.xlsx (xlsx, 112KB), playbook_notes.md (txt, 6KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood offer for Acme — draft (see attached)

Lisa — thank you for the quick turnaround on the RFP. Attached is our draft commercial summary based on the aggressive match approach Marissa recommended. Summary bullets below: 

- Year 1: Match incumbent list for embeddings + blended generative pricing; 12-month committed spend at 70% of historical run-rate.
- One-time migration credit: 8% of Year 1 committed invoice, issued as an invoice credit after go-live.
- Onboarding: two SRE days + up to 40 SE hours included in Year 1 (no additional charge).
- Packaging: two SKUs (Embeddings unit, Generative token unit). No tiered rebates in Year 1 to keep billing simple.
- Termination: standard 60-day notice; data export assistance included.

We can tighten the migration credit into a rebate schedule if Procurement prefers deferred credits; open to splitting into an upfront onboarding credit + remainder tied to usage.

Proposed next step: 30-min commercial call tomorrow at 10:00 PT to resolve packaging questions and sign-off on the commit thresholds. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_offer_acme_v1.pdf (pdf, 24KB)

From: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood offer for Acme — draft (see attached)

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary and the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from Procurement: 

- Packaging: Procurement prefers a blended unit for embeddings + generative in Year 1 to simplify chargebacks across teams. Can Redwood provide a single blended rate option for Year 1 and show math in the next version of the offer?
- Migration credits: the 8% credit is promising, but they'd like 50% as an upfront credit (applied to the first invoice) and 50% deferred against usage over 90 days. Can you accommodate that split?
- Expansion language: if Acme exceeds committed spend by >20% in Year 1, we'd like a 10% overage credit applied to incremental usage. Is that something Redwood can commit to?

We're close — if you can revise the offer with those packaging and credit terms, Procurement will move Redwood into the finalist set for the technical evaluation.

Lisa
Head of AI Procurement
Acme Corp
